title: Unique one-sided K-flat tensor comparison normalized by two-sided descent
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention] and $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K(B)$ be their homotopy category and $Q:K(B)\to D(B)$ localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P_B$ be the full subcategory of K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Use total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and fix the derived tensor and its specified two-sided comparison from [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], written
$$\delta_{T,V}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B V)\xrightarrow{\sim}QT\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}QV\quad(T,V\in\mathcal P_B).$$
For every $T\in\mathcal P_B$, both total tensor functors with fixed factor $T$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms of arbitrary complexes. There is a unique family of isomorphisms
$$c_{T,M}:QT\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}QM\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B M)\quad(T\in\mathcal P_B,\ M\in K(B))$$
which is natural in $M$ and satisfies $c_{T,V}=\delta_{T,V}^{-1}$ for every $V\in\mathcal P_B$. This family is also natural in every homotopy-category map $T\to T'$ between objects of $\mathcal P_B$. Explicitly, for every homotopy-category map $f:M\to M'$,
$$Q(1_T\otimes f)\,c_{T,M}=c_{T,M'}(1_{QT}\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qf),$$
and for every $g:T\to T'$,
$$Q(g\otimes1_M)\,c_{T,M}=c_{T',M}(Qg\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_{QM}).$$
Here composition is written right to left. In particular the first equation holds for every K-flat flat-term resolution $V\to M$ and determines the comparison from its specified two-sided normalization. The analogous assertion for $M\otimes_B T$ holds with normalization supplied by the same two-sided comparison in that order; the chain symmetry interchanging factors has component $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ in bidegree $(i,j)$. The complex $M$ need not be K-flat, termwise flat, or bounded.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), construction immediately preceding the definition: normalized one-sided computation in the specified two-sided localization

proof.text: Total tensor is defined on the homotopy category. In the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], if $f-f'=dh+hd$ in the first variable, $h\otimes1$ is a homotopy between the induced tensor maps: the cross terms cancel because $h$ lowers the first degree by one. In the second variable, a homotopy $k$ induces $(-1)^i1\otimes k$ on the summand of bidegree $(i,j)$, with the same cancellation. Thus both tensor functors and the transformations induced by maps of the other factor are well defined on $K(B)$. The signed interchange $s(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ is a chain isomorphism. Indeed the coefficients of $y\otimes dx$ and $dy\otimes x$ in $sd(x\otimes y)$ are respectively $(-1)^{(i+1)j}$ and $(-1)^{i+i(j+1)}=(-1)^{ij}$, which are their coefficients in $ds(x\otimes y)$. Its square is the identity since $(-1)^{2ij}=1$. The maps are balanced, natural, and pass from presheaf tensors to their sheafifications by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. All calculations act summandwise on direct sums, even for unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact), tensor homotopies; Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), signed interchange

proof.text: Let $f:M\to M'$ be a quasi-isomorphism. The module category is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] makes $C(f)$ acyclic. K-flatness in [def-pc-kflat-complex] gives acyclicity of $\operatorname{Tot}(C(f)\otimes_B T)$. The chain symmetry of step 1 gives acyclicity of $\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B C(f))$. By [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] the latter is the cone of $1_T\otimes f$. The cone criterion again proves this map is a quasi-isomorphism. Conjugating by the natural symmetry proves the same for $f\otimes1_T$. Every homotopy-category arrow has a chain-map representative, so the result holds in $K(B)$ as well. Flatness of the terms of $T$ and boundedness of either complex were not used here.

Write $\mathcal P=\mathcal P_B$ and $L=Q|_{\mathcal P}$. The equivalence $W_B^{-1}\mathcal P\to D(B)$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], compatible with the localization maps, makes $L$ a localization at $W_B$. Explicitly, precomposition with that equivalence is an equivalence on functor categories (precompose with its inverse), and precomposition with $\mathcal P\to W_B^{-1}\mathcal P$ is the equivalence in the definition of localization in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Their composite is precomposition with $L$. Fix $T\in\mathcal P$. Define $F_T:D(B)\to D(B)$ by $F_T(N)=QT\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N$, using the specified tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and $H_T:K(B)\to D(B)$ by $H_T(M)=Q\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B M)$. Step 2 shows that $H_T$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] applied to $Q:K(B)\to D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], choose a functor $\overline H_T$ and a natural isomorphism $\phi_T:\overline H_T Q\xrightarrow{\sim}H_T$. These choices will disappear by uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), construction immediately before the definition; Categories Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization)

proof.text: On $\mathcal P$, put $b_V=\phi_{T,V}^{-1}\delta_{T,V}^{-1}:F_T(LV)\to\overline H_T(LV)$. This is a natural isomorphism: $\phi_T$ is natural and the specified two-sided comparison is natural on homotopy-category maps by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $L$, the functors $F_TL,\overline H_TL$, their displayed descents $F_T,\overline H_T$, and $b$. It gives a unique transformation $\overline b:F_T\to\overline H_T$ restricting to $b$. Apply the same clause to $b^{-1}$; preservation of composition and uniqueness show that the two extensions are inverse. Define $c_{T,M}=\phi_{T,M}\overline b_{QM}$. This is an isomorphism natural in every $M\in K(B)$, and for $V\in\mathcal P$ it equals $\phi_{T,V}\phi_{T,V}^{-1}\delta_{T,V}^{-1}=\delta_{T,V}^{-1}$. Naturality is exactly $Q(1_T\otimes f)c_{T,M}=c_{T,M'}(1_{QT}\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qf)$.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), comparison with the specified two-sided localization; Categories Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), transformation extension

proof.text:
The normalization determines every component, without choosing a comparison map between resolutions. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], for every $M$ choose a quasi-isomorphism $r:V\to M$ with $V\in\mathcal P$. For any family $c'$ natural in $M$ with the required normalization, naturality at $r$ forces
$$c'_{T,M}=Q(1_T\otimes r)\delta_{T,V}^{-1}(1_{QT}\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qr)^{-1}.$$
Both outer factors are isomorphisms: the first by step 2 and the second because $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $F_T$ is a functor. The family of step 4 has the same formula. Hence $c'=c$. This also proves independence of the auxiliary descent in step 3 and that the displayed formula holds for every supplied K-flat flat-term resolution, not only for the chosen one.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor), independence of resolutions with explicit normalization

proof.text:
Let $g:T\to T'$ be any map in $\mathcal P$, not necessarily a quasi-isomorphism. There are two natural transformations $F_TQ\to H_{T'}$, with components
$$a_M=Q(g\otimes1_M)c_{T,M},\qquad b_M=c_{T',M}(Qg\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_{QM}).$$
Their naturality follows from tensor bifunctoriality in step 1 and naturality of $c$ from step 4. At every $V\in\mathcal P$ they agree by the first-variable naturality of $\delta^{-1}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. To extend this equality, choose $r:V\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The common domain map $F_T(Qr)$ is invertible, and naturality gives
$$a_M F_T(Qr)=H_{T'}(r)a_V=H_{T'}(r)b_V=b_M F_T(Qr).$$
Cancel this domain isomorphism. Thus $a_M=b_M$ for every $M$, giving precisely the required naturality in $T$. No inversion of $g$ has occurred.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), simultaneous naturality in the K-flat fixed factor and arbitrary other factor

proof.text:
For the reversed order use $F_T^{\mathrm r}(N)=N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}QT$ and $H_T^{\mathrm r}(M)=Q\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_B T)$. Step 2 proves that the latter inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Repeat step 3 using clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. In step 4 replace $\delta_{T,V}^{-1}$ by $\delta_{V,T}^{-1}$, which is natural in $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and extend the resulting natural isomorphism and its inverse by clause (2). This gives $c^{\mathrm r}_{T,M}$, natural in $M$ and normalized by $c^{\mathrm r}_{T,V}=\delta_{V,T}^{-1}$. For $r:V\to M$ the forced formula is
$$c^{\mathrm r}_{T,M}=Q(r\otimes1_T)\delta_{V,T}^{-1}(Qr\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_{QT})^{-1}.$$
Resolutions exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], so this proves uniqueness exactly as in step 5. For a map $g:T\to T'$, compare $Q(1_M\otimes g)c^{\mathrm r}_{T,M}$ and $c^{\mathrm r}_{T',M}(1_{QM}\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qg)$; they agree at $V$ by naturality of $\delta_{V,T}^{-1}$, and precomposing with the isomorphism $Qr\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_{QT}$ proves equality at $M$, as in step 6. The chain symmetry between the two total tensors is the signed interchange explicitly checked in step 1. Neither construction imposes a condition on the arbitrary complex $M$.
